_provenance: PBR material training against captured reality. The genome is one library entry's appearance params; the measure computes descriptor distances between emitted splat statistics and reference scan statistics. The loop never renders — statistics space only. Final witness is UE substrate.

walls.dist_albedo_mean_luminance: Mean luminance MUST converge to within 15% of the reference scan. Above 15% means the material is perceptually the wrong brightness — a training run that optimized against NOTHING (the pre-fix state). This IS the headline distance: if the mean is wrong, nothing else matters.
walls.dist_roughness_mean: Mean roughness MUST converge to within 20% of the reference scan. A material that is perceptually too smooth or too rough breaks the PBR pipeline — specular response is wrong at every angle.
walls.albedo_mean_luminance: Mean luminance MUST stay in [0.05, 0.90]. <0.05 is vantablack — no PBR material reflects that little diffuse light. >0.90 is fresh snow — physically possible but outside the gamut of most scanned materials. Both extremes indicate the genome has escaped the search space.
walls.roughness_var: Roughness variance MUST stay bounded. Above 0.15 means the material has a bimodal surface — half polished mirror, half sandpaper. That is not a BRDF; it is two materials stapled together.
walls.luma_variance: Luminance variance across splats MUST stay bounded. Above 0.15 means the mottle is so extreme that individual particles read as distinct colors — a glitter effect, not a homogeneous material appearance. A pile of RGB gumballs is not regolith.
walls.albedo_mottle_var: Per-particle albedo spread MUST stay bounded. Above 0.12 means grain-to-grain color variation exceeds what real granular materials exhibit — even mixed regolith has a narrow per-particle gamut.
